mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed in Switzerland; no apostille required, domestic notarization only

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each founder's passport or national identity card
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority of founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Home-country notarization, then Hague Apostille (if the founding state is a Hague Convention member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Evidence of beneficial ownership declaration and UBO register reporting forms
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders and company secretary, supported by Swiss counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified by Swiss notary as part of incorporation deed; no apostille for domestic execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank blocked-capital confirmation (Sperrbestätigung) proving minimum paid-in capital of CHF 50,000
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Swiss bank or Swiss stock exchange bank (UBS, Credit Suisse, systemic or cantonal bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-to-notary direct written confirmation; no legalization required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or incorporation extract for a foreign corporate founder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the state of incorporation; translated into German/French/Italian by certified translator

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all founders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, authorized signatories and controlling persons against: (i) the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions lists and Swiss Embargo Act measures; (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) the OFAC SDN list for any USD exposure and correspondent banking; and (iv) the EU consolidated sanctions list. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) — foreign, domestic and family/associates — must be screened as at-risk categories and escalated for enhanced due diligence under FINMA Circular 2018/03. The screening must be refreshed on every material change in shareholding or management, and all findings must be documented for the AML compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex) at www.zefix.ch; initial preliminary name clearance is requested through the cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) using the e-GRIS / e-Handelsregister electronic filing portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name must be in Latin script, must not be misleading, and must be acceptable in one of the Swiss official languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh); English names are allowed if not deceptive or contrary to public policy. The legal form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' is mandatory and must appear at the end of the name for this entity type.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the cantonal Commercial Register Office rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file an administrative complaint with the competent cantonal supervisory authority within 30 days of receipt of the written rejection. If the cantonal authority sustains the rejection, the applicant may appeal to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) within the statutory appeal period (thirty days). A new or amended name application may be submitted at any time after correcting the defect. Preliminary name reservations may be extended once by filing a request to the Commercial Register Office before the initial 180-day window expires, provided no conflicting entry has been registered in the interim.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are legally permissible as the registered (statutory) office for a Swiss AG provided the service provider offers a physical address in a Swiss municipality, official mail and process-tenant acceptance, registered-address continuity and a minimal physical presence (e.g., meeting room). For a low-risk polyresin statue e-commerce company — a business without a statutory license — a virtual office combined with actual management in Switzerland is generally accepted, but the Registered Office and foreign-ownership rules must satisfy anti-money laundering substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (5-10% within the first two years) for a license-free low-risk ISIC 3240 business. The probability rises to approximately 20-30% if the registered office is a pure virtual mailbox, no operating contract exists, or the company declares UBO data that conflicts with actual management location. Unannounced visits may occur primarily to verify that management files, minutes and books are physically present at the registered office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR; SR 220), Arts. 620–633 (incorporation, shares and minimum capital), Arts. 640–641 (commercial register entry), Arts. 716–716b (board of directors and powers), supplemented by the Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, SR 221.411)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (kantonales Handelsregisteramt) of the registered seat; under the supervisory oversight of the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarially executed Deed of Incorporation (Gründungsurkunde) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten) and the Application for Registration in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung in das Handelsregister), submitted via the eGR online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Aktienkapital of at least CHF 100,000 fully subscribed; at least CHF 50,000 must be paid in before registration in cash through a FINMA-licensed bank blocked account (Sperrkonto), or by approved non-cash contribution evidenced by an audit confirmation under law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators' subscription of CHF 100,000 share capital, allocated as set out in the notarial deed, is ratified; share certificates shall be issued only after full payment. RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at Zurich, Switzerland, and the Board is authorized to lease and equip production premises. RESOLVED, that the first officers, [Chair] and [Secretary], are appointed for a term ending at the first general meeting, each with sole signature authority. RESOLVED, that the Board shall deposit the paid-up capital on a blocked account and complete commercial register registration within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office via the Zefix/eGR portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online preliminary name inquiry to the commercial register of the intended canton, specifying the legal form AG and a business purpose covering manufacture and sale of resin statues and toy kits. Obtain a name reservation where the canton offers this facility; otherwise rely on the registered name clearing at final filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with legal form suffix
Business purpose in line with ISIC 3240
Identity of the founding shareholders or their authorised agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or misleading character, file a revised name by voluntary amendment and re-submit; any IP objection is cured by adopting a distinctive additional word element.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Formation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Civil-Law Notary (Notariat) in the canton of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders appear before the notary with original identification; the notary reads and signs the deed of incorporation, the articles, the list of share subscriptions, and the beneficial-owner declaration. The notary then delivers the certified deed in digital form to the commercial register workflow.
required_dossiers: Passport or official identity certificate for each founder
Exact share subscription and nominal value of share capital
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
List of initial board members and secretary
Beneficial owner declaration in accordance with Art. 628l OR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a statutory defect, the founders execute a rectification addendum and re-sign the deed; the notary may refuse only if the business purpose is objectively unlawful.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-Up Capital Deposit and Bank Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital account in the name of the future AG and transfer the minimum CHF 50,000 paid-in capital from the shareholders. Obtain a written bank confirmation stating that the funds are blocked and will be released to the company upon production of the commercial register extract.
required_dossiers: Certified notarial deed of incorporation
Passport and beneficial ownership data
Source of funds and bank compliance documentation
Company name and anticipated UID number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC issues, provide a sworn statement of source of wealth and a full corporate ownership chart; re-route the transfer to another FINMA-licensed bank if the original refusal persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Public Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) and the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC/SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application through the eGR-register online portal with the notarial deed, articles, bank confirmation, board declaration, beneficial owner declaration, and signature specimens. Pay the statutory registration fee; the register issues the entry decree and arranges the official publication.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed and Articles (certified copy)
Bank confirmation of paid-up capital
Beneficial owner declaration
List of directors and, if required, auditors
Specimen signatures (Unterschriftenblätter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commercial register office issues a deficiency notice, submit the requested supplementary declaration or rectified bylaw within thirty days; failure to cure leads to rejection and requires a fresh application with applicable court remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Social Insurance and Employer Enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Cantonal Tax Office, and cantonal AHV compensation office with SUVA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued commercial register UID, complete the electronic registration forms in the eAdministration portal for VAT (MWST), AHV/atw/EO employer registration, and occupational accident insurance. VAT registration becomes mandatory where taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract and UID confirmation
Passport of directors
Anticipated payroll and salary information
Lease agreement for registered office and production premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a cantonal form is incorrectly completed, file a corrective revision directly with the competent authority before any invoicing activity; statutory 60-day deadlines are counted from the commercial register entry, so act promptly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Industrial and Labour Inspectorate (kantonale Arbeitsinspektorat) and municipal building and fire authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating licence is required for polyresin vacuum casting and hand-painted statue production; municipal building-use permit and fire clearance for the workshop are applicable

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BUWAL) for air and waste; Cantonal Environment Office (Amt für Umwelt) for local permits
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal EIA under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV) for installations below the statutory size threshold; simple environmental compliance for small workshops
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) volatile organic compound limits, generally 100 mg C/m³ in exhaust gas; special waste (uncured resin, contaminated rags, acetone wash) must be disposed of under the Waste Ordinance (VeVA); no untreated resin wastewater may be discharged to sewer

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Feuerpolizeiliche Bewilligung) issued by the municipal fire inspectorate; structural load inspection by a registered engineer for storage racks and workshop floors; workplace safety clearance from SUVA covering painting booths, ventilation and two-exit routes; occupational health attestation for hand-lamination and resin handling

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni ATC) via www.estv.admin.ch and the VAT portal at www.vat.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not established in Switzerland must register for Swiss VAT with the Federal Tax Administration if it supplies services or goods in Switzerland that exceed the statutory turnover threshold. The registration is filed via the online E-Servi portal or the official Form 1040 by a domestic representative. The entity receives a UID number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / Numéro d'identification des entreprises / Numero d'identificazione delle imprese), which serves as the VAT registration number. Registration must be completed no later than 30 days after the commencement of taxable activity. Non-resident entities may be subject to simplified registration and are required to name a Swiss fiscal representative for service of process and tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Swiss tax law. A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is automatically subject to corporate income tax at the federal, cantonal, and communal levels. VAT group registration under Article 15 of the Swiss VAT Act (ORV/OSub/OTVA) may be elected to treat closely linked entities as a single taxable person; the election is optional and requires economic, financial, and organizational integration. No hybrid mismatch election is available for Swiss entity classification purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies, unless the entity is a non-resident supplying services or goods in Switzerland, in which case registration may be required regardless of turnover for supplies that are subject to VAT in Switzerland and not covered by a recovery procedure; voluntary registration is possible under certain conditions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system. VAT invoices must contain mandatory details specified in Article 26 of the Swiss VAT Act and Swiss QR-bill standards are recommended for B2B invoicing. The Swiss Federal Administration has introduced checks on e-bill and QR-bill formats for electronic invoicing but no API-based real-time clearance is required. Retention of electronic records is required for ten years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of goods from Switzerland to foreign destinations is zero-rated for Swiss VAT if the supplier proves that the goods were physically dispatched or transported out of Switzerland. Services related to immovable property abroad, certain intellectual property transfers abroad, and services benefiting the recipient abroad may be zero-rated or outside the scope of Swiss VAT. A direct export must be evidenced by customs declarations and commercial documents showing delivery occurs outside Switzerland; the recipient must be a foreign entrepreneur or final consumer outside Switzerland.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Improper or fraudulent claims for export zero-rating subject the taxpayer to reassessment and collection of unpaid VAT, interest up to 4% per annum, and administrative fines up to three times the tax evaded under Article 57 of the Swiss VAT Act. Criminal penalties for intentional tax evasion can also apply. The Federal Tax Administration audits zero-rating documentation retrospectively and may require production of export proofs, freight contracts, payment records, and foreign importation evidence within statutory limitation periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible. Switzerland maintains no foreign exchange controls and does not differentiate between capital and current account transactions for convertibility purposes. Profit remittance by a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is unrestricted, subject only to standard corporate filing, tax return, and dividend withholding tax procedures; no central bank approval or foreign investment screening applies to ordinary dividend distributions or return of capital. Withholding tax of 35% applies to dividends but is refundable under applicable treaty or Swiss withholding tax relief procedures for eligible recipients.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender rules, mandatory conversion timelines, or required conversion ratios for export receipts in Switzerland. Exporters may retain and freely use foreign currency earnings in domestic or offshore accounts. Compliance obligations are limited to anti-money laundering and tax reporting duties, including accurate declaration of foreign income and maintenance of underlying trade documentation such as invoices, shipping documents, and proof of payment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse (Switzerland) Ltd, now integrated within UBS Group AG

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for offshore digital EMIs that lack a Swiss banking or fintech license. Switzerland allows licensed fintech companies to accept public deposits up to CHF 100 million, but only FINMA-licensed entities may provide payment services to Swiss corporate clients. Offshore EMIs operating under UK or EU e-money licences are not passported into Switzerland; they may provide ancillary payment cards or virtual IBANs but should not be relied upon as the primary treasury or clearing rail. A FINMA-regulated Swiss fintech or a licensed Swiss commercial bank is legally preferable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandatory for a Swiss AG that is already registered in the Commercial Register and has duly authorized directors. Remote onboarding is generally possible through video identification, notarized corporate extracts, and authorized signatory verification. In practice, Swiss banks retain discretion to require a physical or virtual KYC interview with the ultimate beneficial owner and senior management, particularly in respect of the first account opening or significant capital movements. Directors should expect a formal recorded interview, presentation of original passport or certified passport copy, proof of residential address, and explanation of the corporate business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is resident in a jurisdiction outside Switzerland without clear economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart with all UBOs, tax residence certificates, foreign company registry extracts, proof of beneficial ownership chain, minutes of board resolutions confirming the business purpose, and evidence of local substance in Switzerland such as registered office, administration services, and Swiss bank signatory mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of pre-order deposits from retail consumers without standard trade invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: E-commerce merchant agreements, Stripe and PayPal settlement statements, refund policy, order confirmation system documentation, transaction ledger export, general terms and conditions, and a compliance policy on customer due diligence for consumer prepayments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected or actual transactions with persons in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results, transaction counterparty KYC records, commercial invoices with clear description of goods, shipping and customs documentation, end-customer declarations, and internal risk assessment with no-sale or enhanced due diligence thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound equity injection exceeding the registered share capital without clear capital account documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized shareholders' resolution on capital contribution, updated Commercial Register excerpt with current share capital, Swiss bank reference or incoming SWIFT statement, audited or accountant-prepared confirmation of equity funding, and tax declaration of capital contribution reserve.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto-friendly or distributed ledger revenue streams perceived as increasing AML exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Distinct separation of fiat and digital asset ledgers, cryptocurrency transaction monitoring tools, wallet ownership evidence, licencing analysis by a Swiss legal counsel, and a clearly written AML policy covering virtual asset inflows and their conversion into fiat.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be wired via SWIFT MT103 with a clear payment narrative referencing 'equity contribution to Swiss AG' or, where applicable, 'share capital increase'. The beneficiary account should be a Swiss-domiciled corporate bank account in the legal name of the AG. Supporting documentation must include the commercial register excerpt showing authorized share capital, the notarized board and shareholder resolutions, and evidence of the capital contribution entry. Payment purpose codes should use ISO20022 recommendation or SWIFT code categories consistent with equity capital contributions; practical purpose descriptions include 'INVR' for inward investment or 'CAPT' for capital transfer. Banks may request confirmation that the funds are not derived from criminal activity and may require the remitter to pass source of funds checks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for direct wire settlements, commercial letters of credit issued by a Swiss bank for high-value or documentary trade transactions, and SEPA CT for euro-denominated payments inside SEPA. For resin statue sales to retail customers, payout services such as Stripe and PayPal are acceptable as collection rails but should be swept daily to the primary Swiss operating account. Outbound supplier payments should use SWIFT MT103 with commercial invoices, packing lists, and shipping evidence preserved in the trade file. Where the counterparty requires documentary security, an irrevocable commercial LC at sight is recommended with a Swiss advising bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC forward foreign exchange contracts with a Swiss or foreign bank for covered commercial exposures
Currency swaps on a bilateral principal-to-principal basis, commonly EUR/CHF or USD/CHF, allowed for hedging transaction flows
Synthetic or deliverable FX forwards for receipt and payment matching
Cross-currency interest rate swaps only for material treasury liabilities and subject to bank ISDA master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible in rare cases where the counterparty currency is not freely deliverable, though Switzerland's fully convertible CHF regime makes NDFs generally unnecessary

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes and management report if required) approved by the shareholders at the annual general meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No direct government filing; approved accounts are retained at the registered office and must be produced to the cantonal tax authority or auditor on request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No annual late fee; persistent failure exposes directors to personal liability, court-ordered compliance proceedings and, after judicial warning, possible judicial dissolution of the AG.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined federal direct tax, cantonal and communal corporation tax return with signed annual financial statements and tax schedules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung); administers federal direct tax together with cantonal and communal taxes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Common deadline is 30 June following the tax year for calendar-year companies; extensions are available on written request and vary by canton.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines under cantonal procedural law, default interest on tax due, assessment by estimate (ex officio taxation), debt enforcement; not an automatic administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return and payment settlement for taxpayers using the annual filing scheme; quarterly filing remains the default scheme.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), VAT Division.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the close of the annual tax period; for a calendar-year period, due approximately 1 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest from the due date, late-payment penalties, administrative fines up to the statutory maximum, and collection by debt enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AHV (Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance) employer wage declaration, contribution statement and settlement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) responsible for the AG's registered place of business.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual wage declaration is generally required by the final day of January following the wage year, in line with the AHV annual declaration calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, administrative fines or contribution arrears assessed by the compensation office; employer remains liable for unpaid employer and employee contributions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) statutory audit is mandatory for listed or publicly traded AGs and for AGs exceeding in two consecutive years at least two of: balance sheet total CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, or 250 full-time employees. AGs below these thresholds require only a limited audit, but the general meeting may unanimously opt out of audit if the yearly average full-time employee count does not exceed 10.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting law (Art. 958-960) as the statutory framework; Swiss GAAP FER for larger or consolidated reporting; IFRS is permitted and generally required for listed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not impose an annual public UBO return for domestic AGs. The AG must maintain an internal beneficial-owner register under Art. 697j et seq. CO, updated continuously, and preserve the share register (Aktienbuch). Share transfers are effective on entry in the share register; UBO details are confirmed whenever a relevant shareholding transfer occurs and made available to criminal, tax and commercial-register authorities on formal request. No annual UBO certificate is due to the commercial register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managing Officers
General Meeting and Board Minute Book
Beneficial Owner Register (Art. 697j et seq. CO)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - USD 4,500 per year (registered office and corporate secretarial services by canton and fiduciary provider)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - USD 12,000 for a limited statutory audit; nil in years covered by a valid audit opt-out

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax (after-tax equivalent 7.83%); Zug combined effective rate 11.9% (federal 7.83% + cantonal/communal 4.07%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; current preferential instruments: patent/IP box (deduction up to 90% of qualifying IP income), R&D additional deduction up to 50% in participating cantons, notional interest deduction on qualifying equity, participation exemption for dividend and capital gains from qualifying 10%+ shareholdings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 209 (Steuererklärung juristische Personen / tax return for legal entities); filed electronically through the cantonal tax authority's e-portal (e.g. SwissTax / Canton Zug 'Kanton Zug Steuern') with automatic onward transmission to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due 6 months after the end of the business year (for calendar-year taxpayers, by 30 June following the tax year); the cantonal tax authority routinely grants extensions up to 31 October.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net profit before hidden reserves (Reingewinn / résultat net). Insert statutory net income per sworn financial statements, adjusted for non-deductible expenses and tax corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent reporting is not entered here; limited to the Swiss AG's own statutory profit. Apply transfer pricing adjustments for cross-border transactions before completing this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital stock (Aktienkapital) and total par value. Used to compute cantonal capital tax (Zug: approx. 1.5‰ of paid-in capital).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the subscribed capital contributed by the non-resident shareholder at nominal value; capital contribution premium (agio) is reported separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of participations and dividend/capital gains subject to the participation exemption (beteiligungsabzug).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' dividend exemption status is irrelevant at entity level; the AG must attach the country-by-country ownership list and TRC of the ultimate parent if invoking treaty-reduced withholding or DTA benefits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine (Busse) up to CHF 10,000, plus default interest of 4% per annum on the assessed tax from the expiry of the deadline; in wilful concealment, penalty up to 100% of evaded tax and criminal prosecution for tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG (imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to three times the evaded tax).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on any dividend declared by the CH AG, regardless of the recipient's residence; domestic relief exists for qualifying 20%+ participations (Art. 5 VStG) and treaty refunds reduce the rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must (1) obtain an original Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority; (2) file an RD form / Form 218 (Antrag um Rückerstattung der Verrechnungssteuer) with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) within 3 years of the dividend date; (3) demonstrate economic substance and beneficial ownership; and (4) satisfy the Swiss minimum-holding and holding-period requirements of the applicable double taxation agreement (DTA). Upon approval the excess above the treaty rate is refunded.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Swiss WHT domestically (Switzerland does not impose withholding on royalties); treaty rates reduce/eliminate residual Swiss tax if any. Interest: ordinary arm's-length intercompany loans carry 0% WHT; interest from Swiss-issued bonds/money-market instruments is subject to 35% WHT, reduced by DTA rates (generally 0-10%).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed statutory amount in Swiss law; administrative practice under OECD TP guidelines requires a Local File for controlled cross-border transactions exceeding approx. CHF 500,000 per related party per year; a Master File is expected for groups with consolidated annual revenue exceeding CHF 900 million. Transactions below threshold must still be arm's length but full documentation may be waived.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland imposes no annual ESR filing; however, substance is decisive for treaty benefits and withholding tax refunds: a CH AG must maintain at least one registered office, a board meeting at its seat, real staffing, and actual business records in Switzerland. A letterbox/mailbox company claiming DTA relief without personnel or premises will be denied bona fide beneficial ownership and may face tax fraud prosecution. Patent box and R&D incentives additionally require qualifying R&D activity performed in Switzerland.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of taxable income, inflated cost of goods, or false deduction of personal expenses in the AG's tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of at least 25% and up to 100% of the evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG), plus the tax in arrears and default interest; repeated offence raises the minimum to 50%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally sign a false return are jointly and severally liable for the fine under Art. 176 DBG if the AG cannot pay; criminal court may impose travel bans and, upon tax fraud charges, imprisonment up to 6 months.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of forged documents, fictitious invoices, or sham contracts to reduce Swiss taxable income or to obtain fraudulent withholding tax refunds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty under Art. 186 DBG and Art. 14 of the Federal Administrative Criminal Law Act: imprisonment up to 6 months or a fine up to three times the tax evaded, with simultaneous confiscation of forged records. FTA may also enforce 35% withholding on undeclared distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors face personal criminal prosecution; assets can be frozen and foreign travel restricted. If the nominal shareholder is a mere nominee, the individual controlling the AG is treated as the true offender (beneficial owner) and progressively punished.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / abuse of treaty residence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the CH AG solely as a Swiss mailbox to collect IP royalties or dividends while all management, staff, and decisions are outside Switzerland, and then claiming DTA relief on outbound or inbound payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefits and of refund claims for the 35% Swiss withholding tax; tax reassessment with 4% late interest; Swiss FTA additionally reports the ultimate beneficial owner to residence jurisdictions under the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance (MAAC).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the unpaid Swiss withholding tax if they knowingly allowed the AG to distribute profits without withholding or without substance; directive may be issued for provisional seizure and exit from Switzerland (Ausreise) may be prohibited during fraud investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the resin statue business to channel third-party funds, accepting overpriced prepay deposits without delivery, or allowing PayPal/Stripe accounts to be used as payment pass-through for a relative's undisclosed assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code, imprisonment up to three years and fine up to CHF 500,000; violation of mandatory disclosure under Art. 305ter (lack of due diligence) attracts up to one year or fine. Corporate entity liability up to CHF 5 million under Art. 102 CC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ignored the AG's invoicing red flags are held as co-principals under Art. 102 para 2 CC; liable to civil restitution, asset seizure, travel bans pending penal order, and in aggravated cases effective custodial sentences.
